title: Resolve tracker files through the data root in the gate checkers
description:
Makes the gate checkers find tracker files through the data root and keeps their output out of the code checkout's `.jit/`, so that they work from a linked worktree that holds no store and under an inherited tracker environment.

## Background

Three checkers assume the store sits at `.jit/` under the code checkout they run in. The docs-mechanical gate reads `.jit/config.toml` there, copies the code repository's unignored `.jit` files into a scratch directory and runs the projection render in that copy, relying on jit finding the copied store. The research-review gate reads `.jit/references.toml` relative to its working directory. The kani gate writes compressed logs under `.jit/gate-artifacts/`. Two review prompts tell the reviewer to read tracker files at paths relative to the code checkout. The one-shot script `dev/scripts/migrate-link-labels.py` reads issue records and the configuration under the root it is given.

jit selects its store through `JIT_DATA_DIR` and the code checkout through `JIT_WORKTREE_ROOT`, and passes its own environment to a checker. With both set, the scratch render of the docs-mechanical gate would use the live store and write projection targets into the live checkout, while the comparison reads untouched scratch copies and passes. Once the tracker is its own repository mounted at the primary checkout, a gate that runs in a linked worktree finds no store under its checkout.

The data root is `JIT_DATA_DIR` when set, otherwise `.jit` under the top level of the checkout the checker runs in.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The docs-mechanical gate reads the tracker configuration and renders projections from the data root, and gives the same findings for a store under the code checkout and for a store named by `JIT_DATA_DIR` elsewhere.
- [hard] REQ-02: The projection render of the docs-mechanical gate runs against its scratch copy whatever `JIT_DATA_DIR` and `JIT_WORKTREE_ROOT` the gate inherits, and leaves the files of the checkout and of the store unmodified.
- [hard] REQ-03: The research-review gate reads the citation registry from the data root.
- [hard] REQ-04: The kani gate writes its compressed log under the ignored `target/` directory of the checkout it runs in and reports that path; no checker creates `.jit/` in a code checkout.
- [hard] REQ-05: The holistic-review and plan-review prompts name tracker files through the data root.
- [hard] REQ-06: Each changed file under `contrib/gates/` that has a package source under `packages/sim-research/assets/live/` is identical to that source.
- [hard] REQ-07: `dev/scripts/migrate-link-labels.py` reads issue records and the tracker configuration from the data root.
- [hard] REQ-08: The docs-mechanical self-test covers a store outside the code root and a run under inherited `JIT_DATA_DIR` and `JIT_WORKTREE_ROOT`.

## Notes

`contrib/gates/ai-review.sh` reads only the context file jit passes and needs no change. Existing checkouts hold logs under `.jit/gate-artifacts/`, so that directory stays ignored.

planning.outcome: Gate checkers read the store through the data root and write nothing under a code checkout's store path

terminal.test_boundary: docs-mechanical self-test with a store outside the code root
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Path resolution in three checkers, two prompts and one script; one existing self-test extended

title: Run jit against the shared store through one entry point
description:
Adds one tracked entry point that runs jit, or any command, with the tracker environment of the invoking checkout, so that a linked worktree reaches the shared store and gates run in the checkout that started them.

## Background

jit selects its store through `JIT_DATA_DIR` and the code checkout through `JIT_WORKTREE_ROOT`. With only the first set, a gate started from a linked worktree runs in the primary checkout and records the primary's commit. Leases taken from checkouts that share one store differ only by `JIT_AGENT_ID`. jit passes its environment to gate checkers, so a checker started through the entry point inherits these variables; the gate checkers already resolve the store through the data root.

The tracker is to become its own repository mounted at `.jit/` of the primary checkout. A linked worktree then holds no store, and plain jit finds none there. A linked worktree checked out from a commit that still tracks the store holds a stale copy. Until the separation each linked worktree holds its own tracked store and keeps using plain jit.

The entry point is a shell script named `tracker-env` in the scripts directory. It resolves three values and exports them:

- `JIT_DATA_DIR`: `.jit` under the primary checkout, which is the parent of the absolute git common directory.
- `JIT_WORKTREE_ROOT`: the invoking checkout's top level.
- `JIT_AGENT_ID`: the value already set, otherwise `agent:` followed by the name git registers the linked worktree under, which is unique in the repository; in the primary checkout it stays unset and jit uses its configured agent.

Called with a command it executes that command in this environment; called without one it prints the assignments for a shell to evaluate.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Run from a linked worktree whose checkout holds no store, the entry point selects the primary checkout's store and names the linked worktree as code root.
- [hard] REQ-02: Run from the primary checkout, the entry point selects that checkout's store, names that checkout as code root and leaves `JIT_AGENT_ID` as the caller set it.
- [hard] REQ-03: A `JIT_AGENT_ID` set by the caller is passed through unchanged, and two linked worktrees without one get different identities.
- [hard] REQ-04: The entry point exits non-zero and runs nothing when the primary checkout holds no store, with a message naming the missing store, and when the invoking linked worktree holds a store of its own, with a message naming that stale store.
- [hard] REQ-05: The entry point returns the exit status of the command it runs and works when invoked from any directory of the checkout, under `sh`, `bash` and `zsh`.
- [hard] REQ-06: A self-test builds scratch repositories with a primary checkout and linked worktrees with and without a store, covers REQ-01 to REQ-05 without calling jit, passes when the three variables are already set in its environment, and runs as a step of `scripts/cargo-ci.sh`.
- [hard] REQ-07: `.jit/config.toml` sets the worktree root to the checkout that encloses the store, and repository validation passes.

## Notes

The entry point holds no host path: it derives every location from git. Agent guidance names it once the store is separated.

planning.outcome: One script gives each checkout the shared store with its own code root

terminal.consumer_family: agents invoking jit from a checkout
terminal.test_boundary: self-test over scratch repositories run by the CI script
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One shell script, its self-test and one configuration key; no caller changes

title: Refuse a landing whose gate runs record another commit
description:
Adds a check that a lead runs before merging a worker branch: every required gate of the issue must have passed at the tip of that branch. It turns a gate that ran in the wrong checkout from a silent error into a refused landing.

## Background

A gate-run record stores the commit and branch its checker ran at. When jit is started from a linked worktree without the code root set, the checker runs in the primary checkout and the record names the primary's commit; nothing reports this. The issue record itself stores only a gate's status and run identifier. A run that took its verdict from an earlier run launched no checker: it records no commit of its own and names the run that executed the checker. A gate whose checker is built into jit judges the store, not the code, and its run records no commit.

The tracker is to become its own repository, so issue state and code no longer merge together, and the recorded commit is what ties an issue's gate verdicts to the change that lands. While the code repository still tracks the store, recording a gate verdict changes a tracked file, so the branch tip moves after each evaluation and the check cannot pass there; leads apply it from the separation on.

The check is a Python script named `check-landing` in the scripts directory. It takes an issue and a git revision, reads the issue's required gates and the latest run of each through jit's machine-readable output, and compares.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The check exits zero when every required gate's latest run passed and, for each gate whose checker is an executed command, the run that executed it records the commit the given revision resolves to.
- [hard] REQ-02: The check exits non-zero and names the gate, the recorded commit and the expected commit when the run of a gate whose checker is an executed command records a different commit or none, or when any run did not pass.
- [hard] REQ-03: A gate whose verdict was reused from an earlier run is judged by the commit of the run that executed the checker; when that commit differs from the revision, the message states that the gate needs a forced evaluation at the revision.
- [hard] REQ-04: A manual gate is judged by its attestation alone and is listed in the output as attested. A gate with a built-in checker is judged by its pass alone and is listed as store-judged.
- [hard] REQ-05: The check exits with a distinct status and a message when jit is unavailable or the issue does not exist, and never reports success in that case.
- [hard] REQ-06: A self-test covers REQ-01 to REQ-05 against recorded jit output without calling jit, and runs as a step of `scripts/cargo-ci.sh`.

## Notes

The check reads the store only through jit, never through the record files.

planning.outcome: A landing is refused unless each required gate passed at the branch tip

terminal.test_boundary: self-test against recorded gate-status output run by the CI script
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One Python script with an embedded self-test

title: Check tracker references against a mounted store
description:
Makes the reference checker work with and without the tracker: on a clone without it the checker passes and still checks invariant citations, and with the tracker mounted it checks tracker paths and issue prose as it does today.

## Background

`scripts/check-references.py` treats `.jit/` as a root of the code repository. It reads invariant identifiers from `.jit/invariants.toml` and skips that check when the file is absent, scans issue records because the code repository tracks them, and passes any fault whose target git ignores. The tracker is to become its own repository mounted at an ignored `.jit/`. A GitHub runner then has no store: every tracker path named in tracked text would fault, the invariant check would stop silently, and on a host with the store a path to a missing tracker file would pass because `.jit/` is ignored. The invariant projection between the `jit:invariants` markers of `AGENTS.md` lists every invariant identifier and stays in the code repository.

A tracker reference is a path under `.jit/` named in tracked text. The data root is `JIT_DATA_DIR` when set, otherwise `.jit` under the repository root, and the store is mounted when the data root holds a store index. The files of the store are the tracked files and the untracked unignored files of the git repository that contains the data root; that one rule covers a store tracked by the code repository and a store that is its own repository. A linked worktree that reaches a shared store through `JIT_DATA_DIR` sees issue prose written against other branches, so issue prose is checked only where the store sits under the checkout being checked.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: An `@/inv/` or `@/invariant/` citation resolves against the identifiers projected into `AGENTS.md`, with or without a mounted store, and a citation of an unknown identifier faults in both cases.
- [hard] REQ-02: With a mounted store, a tracker reference resolves against the files of the store, and a reference to a missing tracker file faults even when the code repository ignores `.jit/`. A reference to a path that the ignore rules of the store's repository cover passes.
- [hard] REQ-03: Without a mounted store, tracker references do not fault, and the checker prints how many it left unchecked.
- [hard] REQ-04: When the data root is `.jit` under the repository root, the prose of issue records and the archive records are checked under the existing exception rules, whichever repository tracks them. When the data root lies elsewhere, tracker references are checked and that prose is skipped with a printed count.
- [hard] REQ-05: The checker's verdict on the current tree is unchanged, and its self-test covers a tree with the store tracked by the code repository, a tree with the store in its own repository, a tree whose store lies outside the root and is named by `JIT_DATA_DIR`, and a tree without a store. The self-test passes when `JIT_DATA_DIR` is already set in its environment.
- [hard] REQ-06: The module documentation states the resolution rule and the case without a store.

## Notes

The exception entries for tracker paths in `scripts/reference-exceptions.toml` keep their meaning.

planning.outcome: The reference checker passes without the tracker and checks tracker references when it is mounted

terminal.test_boundary: the checker's self-test over four tree layouts
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One checker module: three resolution rules with their self-test cases

title: Mount and snapshot the tracker repository with one command each
description:
Adds the two commands a separate tracker repository needs: one mounts it on a fresh clone of the code repository, one commits a consistent snapshot of the store and pushes it. The store also gains its own ignore rules, which the snapshot relies on.

## Background

jit commits nothing to git. The tracker is to become its own repository at `.jit/` of the primary checkout. A new clone of the code repository then has no store until the tracker is cloned into place, and tracker changes reach the remote only when someone commits and pushes them. Agents write to the store concurrently, so a commit taken between two related writes would record a state jit never published; jit can run a command while it holds the store's write lock. Repository validation resolves each issue's linked documents in the code checkout it runs from, so it fails in one checkout while an issue links a document that exists only on another branch; it cannot gate a snapshot.

Lock files, the worktree identity, server files, gate-run records and gate logs are machine-local and stay uncommitted. Today the root ignore file of the code repository names them; a store that is its own repository needs the rules in `.jit/.gitignore`, which already holds a region that jit owns between its markers.

The mount command is a shell script named `tracker-bootstrap` and the snapshot command one named `tracker-snapshot`, both in the scripts directory.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The mount command clones the tracker repository into `.jit` of the primary checkout, from the URL given as its argument or, without one, from the code repository's `origin` URL with `-tracker` appended to the repository name, and exits zero only when repository validation passes on the mounted store; on a failed validation it leaves the mounted store in place and prints the findings.
- [hard] REQ-02: The mount command refuses, without changing anything, when `.jit` already exists or when it is run from a linked worktree.
- [hard] REQ-03: The snapshot command stages the store's unignored changes, commits them with a subject that states the UTC time and the code repository's `main` commit, and pushes; it stages and commits while jit holds the store's write lock.
- [hard] REQ-04: The snapshot command exits zero without a commit when the store has no change, exits non-zero without a commit when jit refuses the lock, and reports a failed push with a non-zero status while keeping the local commit.
- [hard] REQ-05: The snapshot command refuses when the store directory is not the top level of its own git repository.
- [hard] REQ-06: `.jit/.gitignore` names the machine-local files outside the region jit owns, the root ignore file of the code repository lists no path under `.jit/`, and `git status` in the code repository reports the same files before and after the move.
- [hard] REQ-07: A self-test builds a scratch code repository and a scratch tracker repository with a local remote, covers REQ-01 to REQ-05 with a stand-in for jit, passes when the tracker variables are already set in its environment, and runs as a step of `scripts/cargo-ci.sh`.

## Notes

Both commands reach jit and the store through the tracker entry point. Neither holds a host path or a fixed remote URL.

planning.outcome: A fresh clone mounts the tracker with one command and the store is snapshotted with another

terminal.consumer_family: leads mounting or snapshotting the store
terminal.test_boundary: self-test over scratch repositories with a local remote

title: Write the cutover runbook and rehearse it on a scratch copy
description:
Produces the runbook and the tool that move the tracker out of the code repository, and proves both on a scratch copy before the live cutover.

## Background

The cutover turns `.jit/` of the code repository into an independent tracker repository mounted at the same path. It must carry the history of the tracker paths, lose no tracker state held on a live branch or in a worktree's ignored gate-run records, and leave no checkout with a stale copy of the store. The repository has dozens of linked worktrees, each with its own copy of the store today. Leases live in the git common directory of the repository that holds the store, so they move from the code repository to the tracker repository. The store carries its own ignore rules and worktree root setting, so the extracted tree needs no edit at the mount.

The runbook is a Markdown document named `cutover-runbook` in this epic's directory under `dev/active`, and the tool is a Python script named `cutover` beside it. The linked plan fixes the sequence: quiesce, back up, extract, mount, harvest, verify, clean the worktrees, and roll back on a failed verification.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The runbook states preconditions, numbered steps, a verification step with pass conditions, and a rollback that moves the nested repository aside, reverts the code-side commit and the invariant amendment, restores the tracked store with each tracker change made since the cutover began, and states what becomes of leases taken after the mount.
- [hard] REQ-02: The tool lists each branch and worktree whose tracker files differ from `main`, each worktree that holds gate-run records, and each store with an unreleased lease or a pending redo record. The runbook states how each is merged, harvested or abandoned before extraction, and how the executor's own lease and the control-plane files left in the code repository's git directory are handled.
- [hard] REQ-03: The tool extracts the history of the tracker paths into a new repository whose head tree equals the `.jit` tree of the cutover commit's parent, and fails when the two tree identifiers differ.
- [hard] REQ-04: The tool applies the code-side change in one commit: the tracker paths leave the index, `/.jit/` is ignored, the union-merge attribute and the budget exception for the event log are removed, the reference exceptions for the event log and the citation registry are removed while those for issue prose and archive records stay, tracked paths under `.jit/` become forbidden, and the tree-size limit falls to the measured tree size rounded up to the next 10 kB.
- [hard] REQ-05: The tool replaces `.jit` of the primary checkout with a clone of the new repository and restores the machine-local files; the tracked files of the mounted store are byte-identical to the extracted tree.
- [hard] REQ-06: The tool archives each worktree's store before any deletion, copies a worktree's run records, one file per run, into the shared store and stops on a run record that exists there with different bytes, keeps the store's verdict pointer where a worktree holds a different one for the same gate and inputs and requires that the run each pointer names is in the shared store, merges `main` into a surviving branch with tracker conflicts resolved by deletion, and removes a worktree's local store only after its harvest is verified.
- [hard] REQ-07: A rehearsal on a scratch clone with at least two linked worktrees runs each step and the rollback, and its results are reported in this issue: repository validation, issue count before and after, tree identifiers, a gate evaluated through the entry point from a linked worktree created at the cutover commit recording that worktree's commit, plain jit failing in that worktree, two agent identities holding separate leases, the mount command followed by repository validation on a fresh clone of the scratch code repository, a harvest with a planted verdict-pointer collision, a snapshot and a repository validation from a second checkout while an issue links a document that exists only on an unmerged branch, once unpinned and once pinned to its commit, the self-test steps of `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` run through the entry point from the linked worktree, and both checkers passing on the code tree with and without the store.
- [hard] REQ-08: The rehearsal's outputs stay outside the tracked tree.

## Notes

The rehearsal re-checks four facts the plan takes from the jit documentation: discovery stops at a linked worktree's boundary, a gate records the code root's commit, checkouts sharing the store share one worktree identity, and the worktree root setting resolves to the enclosing checkout for a nested repository. A fact that fails is recorded with the contradiction in this issue before the runbook changes.

planning.outcome: A rehearsed runbook with its tool carries the tracker through the cutover and back

terminal.test_boundary: rehearsal with rollback on a scratch clone holding two linked worktrees
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One runbook and one tool exercised end to end by a single rehearsal; the steps hand over to each other, so a step tested alone proves nothing, and the scripts it calls already exist

title: Execute the tracker cutover
description:
Runs the rehearsed cutover on the live repository: the tracker becomes its own repository mounted at `.jit/` of the primary checkout, and the code repository stops tracking it.

## Background

The runbook and its tool were rehearsed on a scratch copy. The live run needs a quiet repository: no session writes to the tracker, each lease is released, and each live branch is merged or its tracker changes are harvested. The owner provides the remote for the tracker repository, approves the amended wording of the `resolvable-references` invariant and confirms the start.

From the cutover on, agents in a linked worktree reach the store only through the tracker entry point, a lead checks a branch with the landing check before merging it, and the store is committed by the snapshot command. The workflow guidance in `AGENTS.md` is projected from `packages/sim-research/assets/regions/agents-profile-guidance.md` and today names store files at paths relative to the reader's checkout.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `git ls-files .jit` prints nothing on `main`, `/.jit/` is ignored, and the budget checker refuses a tracked path under `.jit/`.
- [hard] REQ-02: The tracker repository's head tree at the mount equals the `.jit` tree of the cutover commit's parent, its history holds the commits of the tracker paths, it is pushed to the owner's remote, and repository validation passes on the mounted store.
- [hard] REQ-03: No worktree holds a local store, no surviving branch tracks a path under `.jit/`, and each gate run record found in a worktree is in the shared store.
- [hard] REQ-04: A gate evaluated through the entry point from a linked worktree created after the cutover records that worktree's commit and branch, and plain jit fails in that worktree.
- [hard] REQ-05: `scripts/tracked-budget.toml` holds no tracker exception and no interim exclusion of the tracker, `.gitattributes` holds no tracker rule, `scripts/reference-exceptions.toml` keeps only the tracker entries for issue prose and archive records, and the tree-size limit equals the measured tree size rounded up to the next 10 kB.
- [hard] REQ-06: `AGENTS.md` and `dev/index.md` state that `.jit/` is the checkout of the tracker repository, how a fresh clone mounts it, that jit runs through the entry point from a linked worktree and where such a worktree finds the store's files, that a branch lands only after the landing check passes, and that a lead snapshots the store after each landing and the steward at the end of a session. `AGENTS.md` stays within 200 lines and its projected regions match their sources.
- [hard] REQ-07: The statement of the `resolvable-references` invariant covers tracker references in the wording the owner approved, and its projection in `AGENTS.md` matches.
- [hard] REQ-08: The reference and budget checkers pass on `main` with the store mounted and on a fresh clone without it, and the reference checker holds no self-test case for a store tracked by the code repository.
- [hard] REQ-09: On a fresh clone of the code repository the build, the fast test tier and each step of `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` that does not call jit pass without the store; the mount command then mounts the tracker and repository validation passes.

## Notes

The cutover commit and the unmount are one step under the canonical-cutover invariant: no commit of `main` tracks the store and ignores it at once. The invariant amendment is committed before the extraction, so the extracted tree carries it. On a failed verification the runbook's rollback applies before any further work.

planning.outcome: The live repository runs on the separate tracker with no tracked or stale store left
